# Reader contract for AI agents

<!-- Generated by `tyto-docs generate --region agents-guide`. Do not edit. -->

Five rules govern how much of this documentation you may rely on, and what to do when
you need more than it offers.

## 1. Claims are orientation

What exists, what owns what, and how the pieces relate. Trust these for navigation and
for deciding where to look. That is what the pages are good at and what they are
checked for.

## 2. For anything task-critical, follow the evidence to source

Every claim-bearing H2 links to an anchor in the page's `<Name>.evidence.md` sidecar.
Each bullet there restates one claim and links to an exact `path#Lstart-Lend` range.
Follow it and read the source. You are about to edit those files anyway.

## 3. A claim with no evidence link is inference

Not verified fact. Treat it as a hypothesis worth checking, not as a premise to build
on. Interview-derived claims are the exception: they link into `DECISIONS.md`, which is
generated from the approved knowledge store, and that anchor is a primary record.

## 4. `written_at_commit` tells you what a page was true for

It sits in the page's frontmatter. Compare it against `HEAD` when it matters — a page
written against an older commit describes the code as it was then, and nothing in this
system silently updates prose when source moves underneath it.

## 5. Generated regions are as current as the last `generate --all`

The module graph, ERD, endpoint list, file table, and navigation are derived
mechanically from source rather than written by anyone. They are exactly as current as
the last time the generators ran, and never more approximate than that.

## Units and ownership

A unit is declared by a component document's `sources` frontmatter. Its document may claim
files from more than one directory, and each source entry records its blob SHA. There is no
central manifest to reconcile; the document owns its own boundary.

Evidence documents are generated by `tyto-docs build-evidence` and are never authored by
a model. If a link is wrong, that is a defect in the generator or in the research it was
built from — not something to fix by editing the sidecar.
